verses.text: After all this, while Artaxerxes was king of Persia, there was Ezra son of Seraiah, whose line went back through Azariah and Hilkiah,
then Shallum, Zadok, and Ahitub,
then Amariah, Azariah, and Meraioth,
then Zerahiah, Uzzi, and Bukki,
then Abishua, Phinehas, Eleazar, and Aaron the chief priest.

That’s the Ezra who went up from Babylon. He was a scribe who knew the law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given. The king granted everything he asked for because the hand of the LORD his God was on him.
In King Artaxerxes’s seventh year, some Israelites went up to Jerusalem, including priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants.
Ezra reached Jerusalem in the fifth month of the king’s seventh year.
He set out from Babylon on the first day of the first month and reached Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month. The good hand of his God was on him.
Ezra had set his heart on studying the LORD’s law, living it out, and teaching its statutes and rulings in Israel.
Here’s a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave Ezra. Ezra was a priest and a scribe trained in the words of the LORD’s commands and statutes for Israel:
“Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the perfect God of heaven. Now,
I’m issuing this order: Any Israelites, priests, or Levites in my kingdom who freely choose to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
The king and his seven advisers are sending you to look into affairs in Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of your God that’s in your hands.
You’re also to carry the silver and gold the king and his advisers freely offered to the God of Israel, whose home is in Jerusalem.
Take all the silver and gold you find throughout the province of Babylon, along with what the people and priests freely give for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
Be quick to use this money to buy bulls, rams, and lambs, along with their grain offerings and drink offerings. Offer them on the altar at your God’s house in Jerusalem.
Use the rest of the silver and gold however you and your fellow Israelites think best, in keeping with your God’s will.
Hand over the vessels you’ve been given for service at your God’s house in the presence of the God of Jerusalem.
If you need to provide anything else for your God’s house, pay for it out of the royal treasury.
I myself, King Artaxerxes, order all the treasurers beyond the River to provide promptly whatever Ezra the priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven asks of you,
up to one hundred talents of silver, one hundred cors of wheat, one hundred baths of wine, and one hundred baths of oil. No limit is set for salt.
Whatever the God of heaven commands, do it exactly for his house. Why bring wrath on the realm of the king and his sons?
We also make it clear that no tribute, customs duty, or toll may be charged to any priest, Levite, singer, gatekeeper, temple servant, or worker at this house of God.
And you, Ezra, use the wisdom your God has given you to appoint magistrates and judges. They’re to judge the people beyond the River who know your God’s laws. Teach anyone who doesn’t know them.
If anyone refuses to obey your God’s law and the king’s law, carry out the sentence promptly, whether it’s death, banishment, loss of property, or prison.”
Bless the LORD, the God of our ancestors! He put it in the king’s heart to make the LORD’s house in Jerusalem beautiful.
He also showed me faithful love before the king, his advisers, and all his powerful officials. The hand of the LORD my God on me gave me strength, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
